report.summary: Chunk 3 of 6: defines analyse_once, build, CSS/JS constants, and helper functions for rendering HTML page components.

handoff.purpose: Define analysis orchestration (analyse_once, build), CSS/JS theme constants, and HTML helper functions (_chip, _section, _narrative_section).

symbols.name: analyse_once
symbols.note: Single walk of the tree; returns (reach report, switch report). Accepts repo_root and optional index; if index is None, calls cached_index with refresh=True.

symbols.name: build
symbols.note: Derives whole payload. Reads tree, snapshot, narrative; writes nothing. Returns dict with schema, root, stamp, counts, reach, switches, gate, narrative.

symbols.name: _THEME_VARS_LIGHT
symbols.note: CSS custom properties for light theme.

symbols.name: _THEME_VARS_DARK
symbols.note: CSS custom properties for dark theme.

symbols.name: _CSS
symbols.note: Complete CSS string with light/dark theme variables and all page styles.

symbols.name: _TOGGLE_JS
symbols.note: IIFE that creates a theme toggle button and appends it to #stampbar.

symbols.name: _chip
symbols.note: Returns a <span> with class 'chip s-{status}' and optional title attribute.

symbols.name: _section
symbols.note: Returns a <section> with id, <h2>, and body.

symbols.name: _narrative_section
symbols.note: Returns a <section> with narrative content if present and non-empty; otherwise returns empty string or fallback.

claims.text: The single walk of the tree. Returns ``(reach report, switch report)``.
claims.why: Function returns tuple of reach_mod.analyse and switches_mod.analyse results.

claims.text: Extracted so that ONE analysis can serve the page, the gate and the re-baseline inside a single ``daedalus map`` run.
claims.why: No code in chunk shows usage of analyse_once by page, gate, or re-baseline.

claims.text: When they were three calls they were also three chances to disagree, and they took them: the page reported six islands while the gate on the same page reported eleven, with not one member in common.
claims.why: Anecdotal claim; no code in chunk references previous behaviour.

claims.text: refresh=True on purpose. ``cached_index`` memoises per process, and this map's whole value is that it describes the tree NOW -- a map served from an index some earlier caller in this process warmed would be exactly the silently-stale artifact the command exists to replace.
claims.why: Comment about cached_index behaviour; cached_index not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: The on-disk cache is content-keyed, so the rebuild is still cheap.
claims.why: Claim about on-disk cache; no code in chunk verifies this.

claims.text: Derive the whole payload. PURE with respect to the repository: it reads the tree, the snapshot and the narrative, and writes nothing.
claims.why: Function body only reads files (Path, load_narrative) and returns dict; no write operations.

claims.text: The theme toggle stamps data-theme on <html>, and BOTH data-theme rules are emitted so the toggle wins in either direction: a viewer whose OS says dark must be able to force light, which a bare prefers-color-scheme block cannot do.
claims.why: _CSS contains :root[data-theme="dark"] and :root[data-theme="light"] rules, and _TOGGLE_JS sets data-theme attribute.

observations.what: The analyse_once function imports reach_mod and switches_mod from relative imports; these modules are not defined in this chunk.
The build function uses drift_mod.check and expects a snapshot path; drift_mod is imported locally within build.
The build function calls git_stamp with scanned argument; git_stamp is not defined in this chunk.
The _narrative_section function calls _render_md which is not defined in this chunk.
The CSS constant _CSS uses .replace('__LIGHT__', _THEME_VARS_LIGHT).replace('__DARK__', _THEME_VARS_DARK) to inject theme variables.
The _TOGGLE_JS script appends a button to an element with id 'stampbar'; that element is expected to exist in the HTML.
The build function's return dict includes a 'gate' key with fields 'ok', 'first_run', 'snapshot_path', 'snapshot_exists', 'state', 'counts', 'items', 'blocking', 'text'.
